newsitem.title: ITALY: Edison attacks Eni-Enel electricity plan.
newsitem.headline: Edison attacks Eni-Enel electricity plan.

text.p: Italy's planned electricity production joint venture between Eni and Enel could create a barrier to the entry of other producers into the market, Edison MD Giulio Del Ninno said.
This would obstruct the liberalisation of the electricty sector in Italy, Del Ninno said at the inauguration of Edison's new Cet 3 power plant at a steel producing plant at Taranto.
Edison, Italy's largest non state-owned electricity producer, is the energy unit of agrichemical group Montedison.
State-controlled energy group Eni and electricity utility Enel plan to set up the country's largest independent electricity production company.
The two groups said the new company would have initial output capacity of 5,000 Megawatts -- around a third of Italy's free market needs. Edison has installed power of some 3,200 Megawatts.

"A company (like the Eni-Enel one) with a capacity of up to 8,000 Megawatts represents nearly half the potential of the future free market and can therefore represent a barrier for others. It would be important to avoid this, as the electricty sector watchdog authority has already said," Del Ninno said.

The Taranto power station is owned by ISE, a company 75 percent controlled by Finel (a joint venture between Edison with 60 percent and Electricite de France (EDF) with 40 percent) and 25 percent held by Italy's private Riva group.

Cet3, which has involved investment of one trillion lire ($588.2 million), is the world's first large-sized (505 Mw) electricity generating plant which recovers gases from the steel-producing process to produce electric power and steam.
Del Ninno said Edison plans total investments of 450 billion lire in 1997 and 400 billion in 1988 after investing 700 billion lire in 1996.
